reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-provided parameter 'param' which flows through doSomething() and gets encoded in HTML context, but the encoding happens after the tainted data reaches the response sink. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-provided parameter 'param' which directly influences the file path construction in the File constructor. Both alerts are exploitable as they involve user-controllable data reaching security-sensitive sinks.

evidence.note: User input retrieved via getParameterMap and assigned to param

File constructed using bar (which is param) as part of path
Response sink with bar (user input) concatenated into HTML output
